title: White chicken chili
subtitle: Chicken, white beans, and green chilli stew with soured cream
excerpt: White chicken chili is a mild, cream-enriched stew of shredded chicken thighs, white beans, green chillies, and cumin. It gets its name from the absence of tomatoes and red chilli: the broth stays pale gold and slightly thick from the beans. A spoonful of soured cream and a handful of crushed tortilla chips finish it.
sourceNotes: American culinary tradition. White chicken chili became popular in the United States in the 1990s as a lighter alternative to beef red chili. Documented in mid-1990s American food magazines and general cookbooks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the soured cream garnish for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make entirely ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently: the soured cream curdles if it boils.

content.text: White chicken chili is a gentle, warming stew: shredded chicken, cannellini or haricot beans, green chillies, cumin, and chicken stock, finished with soured cream to give the broth a creamy body. The colour stays pale. The heat is mild to medium. It comes together in about 40 minutes and the leftovers are excellent.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of garlic, {{chilli-green}} green chillies, {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, and {{oregano-dried}} of oregano. Cook for 1 minute. Add the {{chicken-thighs-boneless}} chicken thighs and {{stock-chicken}} of stock. Bring to a simmer and cook covered for 25 minutes.

Lift out the chicken and shred with two forks. Mash a third of the {{cannellini-beans}} of drained cannellini beans to a paste and stir into the broth to thicken it. Add the remaining whole beans and the shredded chicken. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Stir in {{soured-cream}} of soured cream. Do not reheat after adding the cream. Add the lemon juice and season with salt. Serve with coriander and crushed tortilla chips.

items.fix: Take the pan off the heat before adding the soured cream. If reheating leftovers, add a fresh spoonful of soured cream at the table rather than in the pot.
Mash a generous third of the beans before adding them back. This thickens the broth without cornflour.

content.text: A teaspoon of chipotle paste in place of fresh green chilli gives a smokier result. Sweetcorn stirred in at the end adds sweetness. The dish works well in a slow cooker: 6 hours on low, shred the chicken, add the beans and cream at the end.

White chicken chili emerged as a lighter American chili in the 1990s and became a winter weeknight staple across the country. It lacks the deep regional roots of Texas red or New Orleans red beans, but it has earned its place in the weeknight repertoire.
